questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests the ability to implement tenant-scoped security policies inside a CNF gateway, using Kubernetes ConfigMaps for policy storage and a sidecar for real-time evaluation. It also checks understanding of config reloads and per-request performance.

## Key Concepts

- Tenant-aware policy evaluation and path/method matching
- Sidecar design and ConfigMap-driven policy
- In-memory policy cache and reload semantics
- Path normalization and wildcard handling

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo: evaluatePolicy(tenant, method, path) -> boolean
function evaluatePolicy(tenant, method, path) {
  const rules = policy[tenant] || []
  for (const r of rules) {
    if (r.method === method && (r.path === path || matches(r.path, path))) return true
  }
  return false
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle overlapping rules or wildcard policies across tenants?
- How would you audit and rotate policies without downtime?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a compliant telemetry stack for CNF gateways with multi-tenant segregation and data privacy.

## Key Concepts
- Telemetry pipelines (OpenTelemetry, Fluent Bit) across logs and traces
- Tenant context propagation and isolation
- PII masking via in-line filters (e.g., Lua) before forwarding
- Loki/Jaeger exporters and per-tenant pipelines

## Code Example
```yaml
# Fluent Bit ConfigMap snippet (Lua filter used for masking)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: fluent-bit-pp
data:
  lua-filter.lua: |
    function filter(tag, dt)
      if dt["message"] ~= nil then
        dt["message"] = (dt["message"]):gsub("%w+@%w+%.%w+", "[REDACTED_EMAIL]")
      end
      return dt
    end
```
```yaml
# OTEL collector snippet (simplified)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: otel-collector-config
data:
  collector.yaml: |-
    receivers:
      otlp:
        protocols:
          grpc: {}
          http: {}
    processors:
      attributes:
        actions: [insert]
        keys: [tenant_id]
        from_context: true
    exporters:
      jaeger: {}
      loki: {}
    service:
      pipelines:
        traces:
          receivers: [otlp]
          processors: [attributes]
          exporters: [jaeger]
        logs:
          receivers: [otlp]
          processors: [attributes]
          exporters: [loki]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test cross-tenant leakage in logs/traces?
- What metrics would verify isolation and masking effectiveness?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests design of a tenant-isolated shadow traffic feature, ensuring production safety and auditability.

## Key Concepts
- Sidecar pattern, ConfigMaps, per-tenant routing, traffic shadowing, sandbox namespace.
- Hash-based sampling, header preservation, observability.

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: shadow-config
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  shadow.json: |
    { tenantID: tenant-a, percent: 20, sandboxNamespace: shadow-tenant-a }
```

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: cnf/gateway:latest
      - name: shadow-sidecar
        image: cnf/shadow-sidecar:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: shadow-config
          mountPath: /etc/cnf/shadow.json
        env:
        - name: SHADOW_CONFIG
          value: /etc/cnf/shadow.json/shadow.json
      volumes:
      - name: shadow-config
        configMap:
          name: shadow-config
```

- How would you verify shadow traffic without affecting production SLAs?
- What are the edge cases if tenant churn or sandbox namespace cleanup?

## Why This Is Asked

This question assesses practical knowledge of traffic management in multi-tenant environments. It tests understanding of Istio's traffic splitting capabilities, header-based routing, and safe rollout strategies. Candidates must balance per-tenant isolation against system complexity.

## Key Concepts

- **Istio traffic management**: DestinationRules define service subsets; VirtualServices handle routing rules
- **Canary deployments**: Gradually shift traffic between versions to validate changes safely
- **Header-based routing**: Use x-cluster-local headers or custom headers like X-TENANT-ID to identify tenants
- **Weight-based traffic splitting**: Distribute traffic percentages across subsets

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: DestinationRule
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway-dr
spec:
  host: cnf-gateway
  subsets:
  - name: prod
    labels:
      version: prod
  - name: canary
    labels:
      version: canary
---
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway-vs
spec:
  hosts:
  - cnf-gateway
  http:
  - match:
    - headers:
        x-tenant-id:
          exact: canary
    route:
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway
        subset: canary
      weight: 15
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway
        subset: prod
      weight: 85
  - route:
    - destination:
        host: cnf-gateway
        subset: prod
```

## One-Namespace Test Validation

```yaml
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: canary-test
  labels:

---

    matchLabels:
      app: cnf-gateway
      version: prod

    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gateway
        version: prod
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: cnf-gateway:v1
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: cnf-gateway
  namespace: canary-test
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 8080
  selector:
    app: cnf-gateway
```
